title: Ledger and Orchard
premise: In the port city of Vellmark, where the Halvard Trading Company keeps its ledgers more carefully than its workers, Ivo Voss discovers that a census question about 'unregistered dependents' is actually a purge list — children like her, born to divers and dockhands, are being quietly erased from the record so their indentures can be sold without consent. When the census taker, Anselm, defects and hands her his notes, Ivo must smuggle the true count of the company's hidden laborers into the archive of the rival Kestrel Guild before the Company's historians can certify a falsified register. She wins, but at the cost of Anselm's life and her own name: the truth enters history under an alias she chooses for every erased child, while Ivo Voss remains officially nonexistent — free, and unrecorded.
about_author: I. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging shipping manifests in northern European ports. Their fiction explores what paperwork remembers when people cannot.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Ivo Voss, seventeen and indentured to the Halvard Trading Company since her pearl-diver mother drowned, answers the census taker's routine questions until he asks how many 'unregistered dependents' sleep in the divers' barracks. His pen hovers; his face goes pale. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in her belief that history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: Ink Weighs More Than Water
chapters.summary: Ivo watches the census taker, Anselm, return at night to correct his own entries, striking names from the rolls. She confronts him; he confesses the census feeds a falsified register that legally converts erased children into transferable property. POV: Ivo, with Anselm's confession as centerpiece. Emotional beat: vertigo — survival itself was a clerical error she's about to inherit.

chapters.title: What the Barracks Know
chapters.summary: Ivo tests Anselm's claim against memory: missing playmates, mothers who 'went inland,' a barracks roster that never grows though children do. The older divers warn her to stop counting. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose — the erasure has been happening her whole life, to everyone she loved.

chapters.title: Anselm's Defection
chapters.summary: Anselm copies his private notes — years of true counts — and gives them to Ivo, asking only that they reach the Kestrel Guild archive before the Company certifies its register at month's end. Company stewards begin asking after him. POV: alternating Ivo and Anselm. Emotional beat: terrified hope, and the weight of becoming someone else's witness.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: To move freely between districts, Ivo trades her mother's last pearl to a smuggler who demands a favor in return: identifying which warehouse holds the Company's sealed original ledgers. She agrees, knowing betrayal is now a tool she owns. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: corruption's first taste — power offered cheaply, priced later.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Entries
chapters.summary: Anselm is detained by Company historians who offer him rehabilitation in exchange for recanting. He stalls, buying Ivo time but burning his own. Through a barred window he watches his life's work carried out in crates — toward the furnace, not the archive. POV: Anselm. Emotional beat: quiet resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: The smuggler reveals his price: not the ledgers' location, but Ivo herself, delivered to the Company as the informant who caught Anselm. She escapes through the flooded cellar district using diver's breathing techniques her mother taught her. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: fury and clarity — every hand extended has been a ledger entry.

chapters.title: Certification Day
chapters.summary: The Company convenes to certify its falsified register before guild witnesses. Ivo infiltrates with the smugglers' warehouse crew, swaps the certified copy for Anselm's true counts mid-ceremony, and watches a Kestrel archivist read aloud a number that cannot be explained away. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: climax — triumph laced with terror as guards close in.

chapters.title: What Anselm Paid
chapters.summary: Anselm takes full blame for the falsification, claiming he altered the census alone; his public execution buys legal cover for the true register's acceptance. Ivo, unrecognized in the crowd, understands she is the debt he chose to pay. POV: Ivo, watching. Emotional beat: devastation transmuted into obligation — justice arrived wearing a dead man's name.

chapters.title: Signed With No Name
chapters.summary: Months later, the Kestrel archive accepts the corrected count under the alias Ivo submitted: 'the Children of the Orchard,' her mother's word for the barracks kids. Officially, Ivo Voss does not exist — no record, no owner, no name. She walks the docks free and unrecorded, keeping the one ledger that matters in her head. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — survival outside the law, remembrance outside history.
